what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 2: Corrigendum packet for PR #8146. A probe found and another model family confirmed this defect in PR #8146: S1's iff 'the majority of a 2:1 triple is most likely iff p > max(q,r)' fails at (5,2,4) for the antipodal pattern: p > max(q,r) does not imply p^2 q > r^3. TASK: (a) the minimal corrected statement (the largest domain on which the original holds, or the corrected formula), proved; (b) every later statement in that note AND in other notes of the campaign that uses the defective one (search the PR branches of blocks 12-35: PRs #8146-#8180), with a verdict for each: unaffected / holds on the corrected domain / needs its own repair; (c) the exact lines of the note and runner that must change. check.py verifies the corrected statement exactly and exhibits the original's failure. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/corrigendum-PR8146/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/corrigendum-PR8146/<name>/check.py"
